properties.name: French Polynesia
properties.explanation: France colonized Tahiti in 1842 and conducted 193 nuclear tests there (1966-1996), contaminating islands and sickening residents. Indigenous Mā'ohi are about 78% of population but France controls defense, foreign policy, and justice. The UN lists French Polynesia as a non-self-governing territory.

properties.name: DR Congo (Batwa/Pygmy)
properties.sources: Forest Peoples Programme; Minority Rights Group International

properties.name: Xinjiang (Uyghur Region)
properties.sources: UN Human Rights Office assessment (August 2022); Chinese Census

properties.name: Libya
properties.explanation: Italy colonized Libya in 1911, settled 150,000 Italians, and killed tens of thousands of Libyans in concentration camps. After independence in 1951, settlers remained until Gaddafi expelled them in 1970. Libyans now control their own country.

properties.name: Tibet
properties.sources: Human Rights Watch; International Campaign for Tibet

properties.name: Myanmar (Karen, Kachin, Shan, Others)
properties.sources: UN Human Rights Council; UN Fact-Finding Mission on Myanmar

properties.name: Philippines (Lumad, Igorot)
properties.sources: Global Witness; UN Special Rapporteur; Karapatan

properties.name: Sápmi (Sámi Territories)
properties.sources: Norwegian Supreme Court (Fosen, 2021); UN Special Rapporteur; Sámi Council

properties.name: Angola
properties.explanation: Portugal colonized Angola and settled 400,000 Portuguese by 1975. After the independence war, most settlers fled. Despite a devastating civil war (1975-2002), Angolans now control their own country.

properties.name: Venezuela
properties.sources: Venezuelan Census; UN Human Rights Council

properties.name: Namibia
properties.explanation: German settlers committed genocide against Herero and Nama peoples (1904-1908). South Africa then ruled until independence in 1990. Today, the indigenous majority governs, but white Namibians still own most commercial farmland. Germany acknowledged the genocide in 2021. Land reform is ongoing.

properties.name: South Africa
properties.sources: South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission; Statistics South Africa

properties.name: Central African Republic (Aka/Bayaka)
properties.explanation: The Aka (Bayaka) people—indigenous forest dwellers—face displacement from logging and conservation projects. They are ethnically and culturally distinct from the Bantu-speaking majority. Armed conflict has worsened their situation. The Aka have no formal land rights recognized by the state.

properties.name: West Papua
properties.sources: UN Human Rights Council; Amnesty International

properties.name: Mozambique
properties.explanation: Portugal colonized Mozambique and settled Portuguese in cities and on plantations. After independence in 1975, most settlers left. Mozambicans now govern themselves.

properties.name: Kenya (Ogiek, Sengwer, Maasai)
properties.explanation: Indigenous groups face ongoing evictions for conservation. The Ogiek were evicted from the Mau Forest; in 2017, the African Court ruled this violated their rights, but evictions continue. The Sengwer face violent evictions from Embobut Forest. Maasai have lost land to national parks.
properties.sources: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights (2017); Amnesty International

properties.name: Pakistan (Balochistan)
properties.sources: Human Rights Watch; UN Human Rights Council

properties.name: Republic of Congo (Forest Peoples)
properties.explanation: Indigenous peoples (Aka, Baka, and others) face displacement from logging and conservation projects. They are ethnically distinct from the Bantu majority. A 2011 law recognized indigenous rights, but implementation is weak. Logging companies operate on ancestral lands.

properties.name: Western Sahara
properties.sources: UN list of Non-Self-Governing Territories; MINURSO

properties.name: Zimbabwe
properties.explanation: British settlers ruled as Rhodesia until 1980. After independence, land reform transferred most white-owned farmland to Black Zimbabweans. The white population dropped from 296,000 to about 30,000. This is 'decolonizing' because settlers lost both political power and most of their land.

properties.name: Cuba
properties.explanation: Spanish settlers exterminated nearly all indigenous Taíno people through violence, disease, and forced labor within decades of 1492. The island was then populated by Spanish settlers and enslaved Africans. Indigenous Taíno were eliminated—this is a completed settler colonial project.

properties.name: Gabon (Baka)
properties.explanation: Baka and other indigenous forest peoples face displacement from national parks and logging concessions. Gabon has created many protected areas, but indigenous peoples who lived in these forests for generations were not consulted and have been pushed out.

properties.name: Nepal (Janajati)
properties.explanation: Nepal's 59 recognized Janajati (indigenous) groups—about 35% of the population—have been marginalized by Hindu high-caste dominance. The state was built on their exclusion. Federal restructuring in 2015 was supposed to address this, but indigenous representation and land rights remain contested.
properties.sources: IWGIA; Nepal Federation of Indigenous Nationalities

properties.name: Bahamas
properties.explanation: The indigenous Lucayan people were completely eliminated by Spanish slavers within 25 years of Columbus's 1492 arrival—the islands were left empty. Britain later colonized with settlers and enslaved Africans. The entire current population descends from this later settlement.

properties.name: Tunisia
properties.explanation: France established a protectorate in 1881 and European settlers took significant land. After independence in 1956, the settlers left. Today, Tunisians control their own country. The settler colonial period ended.

properties.name: Hawaii
properties.explanation: American businessmen overthrew the Hawaiian Kingdom in 1893 using US Marines. Congress officially apologized for the illegal overthrow in 1993—but Hawaii remains a US state. Native Hawaiians are now only ~10% of the population in their own homeland. The US government controls the islands.

properties.name: Cameroon (Baka/Bagyeli)
properties.explanation: Baka and Bagyeli peoples—indigenous forest dwellers distinct from the Bantu majority—have been evicted from their ancestral forests for logging concessions and national parks. WWF-funded anti-poaching patrols have committed documented abuses against Baka communities.

properties.name: Nicaragua
properties.sources: UN Human Rights Office; Oakland Institute

properties.name: Botswana (San/Bushmen)
properties.sources: Botswana High Court ruling (2006); Survival International; UN CERD

properties.name: Guatemala
properties.sources: UN Commission for Historical Clarification (CEH); Guatemalan Census

properties.name: Suriname
properties.explanation: Dutch colonizers brought enslaved Africans and indentured laborers from India, Indonesia, and China. Indigenous peoples (about 4% of population) were displaced to the interior. The government is controlled by descendants of colonial-era migrants. Indigenous land rights are poorly protected.

properties.name: Liberia
properties.explanation: Freed American slaves settled here starting in 1822 and dominated the indigenous population for 130+ years—a unique case of Black settler colonialism. Americo-Liberians controlled the government until a 1980 coup. Today, indigenous Liberians hold political power. The settler minority lost control.

properties.name: Georgia (Abkhazia & South Ossetia)
properties.sources: UN; OSCE; Human Rights Watch; European Court of Human Rights

properties.name: Costa Rica
properties.explanation: Spanish settlers colonized Costa Rica and their descendants control the country today. Indigenous peoples are about 2% of the population and live mostly in designated territories, but these lands face encroachment from non-indigenous settlers.

properties.name: Dominican Republic
properties.explanation: Spanish settlers eliminated the indigenous Taíno population through violence, disease, and enslavement within decades of Columbus's 1492 arrival. The country was then populated by Spanish settlers and enslaved Africans. The indigenous population was completely replaced.

properties.name: Vietnam (Central Highlands)
properties.explanation: After 1975, Vietnam's government settled ethnic Vietnamese (Kinh) in the Central Highlands through 'New Economic Zones,' turning indigenous Montagnard/Degar peoples (Jarai, Rade, Bahnar) into minorities. Montagnards face land confiscation and religious persecution. Many have fled as refugees.

properties.name: New Caledonia (Kanaky)
properties.sources: UN list of Non-Self-Governing Territories; French government

properties.name: Ukraine (Donbas - Pre-2022)
properties.sources: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine; OSCE

properties.name: Crimea
properties.explanation: Stalin deported the entire Crimean Tatar population in 1944, killing 18-46% during the deportation. Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, has since moved more Russian settlers in, banned the Crimean Tatar Mejlis, and persecutes Tatars who resist. Russia is actively settling the territory it seized.
properties.sources: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine; OSCE

properties.name: Belize
properties.sources: Caribbean Court of Justice (2015); Belize Census

properties.name: Wallis and Futuna
properties.explanation: France controls this Pacific territory, which is on the UN list of non-self-governing territories—meaning it is officially recognized as a colony. The indigenous Polynesian population (95%+) maintains traditional chiefs, but France has ultimate authority.

properties.name: Ethiopia (Lower Omo Valley)
properties.explanation: The Ethiopian government forcibly relocated indigenous peoples (Mursi, Bodi, Kwegu, Kara) from the Lower Omo Valley for the Gibe III dam and state sugar plantations. Traditional flood agriculture was destroyed. These groups are ethnically distinct from the Amhara and Oromo majority.

properties.name: Jamaica
properties.explanation: Spanish settlers eliminated the indigenous Taíno, then Britain took over and brought enslaved Africans. The indigenous population was completely replaced. Jamaica gained independence in 1962, but this was a post-indigenous society—the original people were already gone.

properties.name: Israel
properties.sources: UNRWA; UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

properties.name: Bangladesh (Chittagong Hill Tracts)
properties.explanation: The government deliberately settled 400,000 Bengalis in the Chittagong Hill Tracts between 1979-1984, turning indigenous Jumma peoples (Chakma, Marma, Tripura) into a minority in their homeland. A 1997 peace accord promised to address this, but settlers remain and land grabbing continues.
properties.sources: Chittagong Hill Tracts Commission; Amnesty International; IWGIA

properties.name: Burundi (Batwa)
properties.explanation: The Batwa of Burundi—the original inhabitants before Hutu and Tutsi arrived—have been pushed out of forests and denied land rights. They comprise about 1% of the population and face severe discrimination. The Batwa are landless and excluded from political participation.

properties.name: Azerbaijan (Nagorno-Karabakh - Historical)
properties.sources: Human Rights Watch; International Crisis Group; UNHCR

properties.name: Trinidad and Tobago
properties.explanation: Spanish colonizers eliminated most indigenous peoples, then Britain brought enslaved Africans and later indentured laborers from India. Today's population descends from settlers, enslaved people, and indentured laborers—not the original inhabitants.

properties.name: American Samoa
properties.explanation: The US has controlled American Samoa since 1900. Samoans are US 'nationals' but not citizens—they cannot vote for president. The UN lists it as a non-self-governing territory. Traditional land ownership has been preserved, but the US federal government still has ultimate authority.

properties.name: Puerto Rico
properties.explanation: Spain colonized Puerto Rico in 1493, eliminating most of the indigenous Taíno population. The US seized it in 1898 and still controls it today. Puerto Ricans cannot vote for US president and have no voting representation in Congress. The UN lists Puerto Rico as a colony.

properties.name: Northern Cyprus
properties.sources: UN Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus; European Court of Human Rights

properties.name: West Bank (Israeli Settlements)
properties.sources: UN Security Council Resolution 2334; B'Tselem; Peace Now

properties.name: US Virgin Islands
properties.explanation: The indigenous Taíno and Kalinago were eliminated by Spanish colonizers. Denmark then colonized using enslaved Africans. The US purchased the islands in 1917. Today's population descends from enslaved people and later migrants, not indigenous inhabitants.

properties.name: Guam
properties.explanation: Spain colonized Guam in 1668, devastating the indigenous Chamorro population. The US seized it in 1898. Today, the US military controls 29% of the island. Chamorros are only 37% of the population—a minority in their homeland. The UN lists Guam as a colony.
properties.sources: UN list of Non-Self-Governing Territories; US Census

properties.name: Barbados
properties.explanation: The island had no indigenous population when the British arrived in 1627. Britain established sugar plantations using enslaved Africans. The entire population descends from colonial-era settlers and enslaved people. This is a fully settler-created society.
